10/9/2024 Today we talked about: Little LadyBriefly, what behaviors are you concerned about?: Consistently barking/lunging/jumping when someone else *stops* petting her. Inconsistently the same for some people at a bit of a distance, still trying to figure out if her trigger is men, someone approaching her while on a leash, or overstimulation in general. No actual violent aggression though with some dog savvy folks i'm testing with, just big feelings! <3Work on basic manners, impulse control, and redirection.Working on confidence will be a huge benefit. Basic training will help with that! Here are some great links to work on Five Mini-Basics videos (basic skills to set them up for success!) She jumps at sudden noises and movements, seems easily startled, and lacks confidence in open spaces, often tucks her tail between her legs. With consistent positive reinforcement, gentle exposure, and time, I believe she can become much more comfortable outside. AD is the absolute sweetest. She did fantastic on our outing today! Some notes from our day out: she was pretty good on leash - pulls towards all humans and dogs for pets and greetings but is generally easy to manage. We met a couple on our walk who had adopted two dogs from FCAS and AD had good interactions with both of them. I brought her into my house briefly to see what reaction she would have to my cat - she had no reaction at all from about 10 feet away. By no means conclusive, but a positive indicator of her cat friendliness. I think AD could get adopted quickly with some additional exposure. She has been at the shelter for two months and has never been very visible. She started out in a kennel across from the clinic and is now in 67 on the B side (which is too small for her). Potential foster coming back the following Wednesday for pick up. LB
